name: Adoni-bezek
overview: Adoni-bezek was a male figure known as the lord of Bezek, a title indicating his rulership or authority over that location. A notable and unique attribute of Adoni-bezek is that his thumbs and big toes were cut off, a detail recorded in the book of Judges. There is no information on his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Adoni-bezek means 'lord of Bezek,' directly reflecting his position as a ruler. This proper name is not indicated to have been given by God but identifies his status in the biblical narrative as recorded in Judges 1:5.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Adoni-bezek beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as lord of Bezek. No further relational information is provided.
scriptureSignificance: Adoni-bezek's significance in Scripture centers on his role as a local ruler whose defeat and subsequent maiming demonstrate the consequences of his actions and the justice administered during Israel's conquest. The removal of his thumbs and big toes symbolizes a divinely permitted judgment and serves as a poignant example of God's sovereignty in the unfolding history of Israel as narrated in Judges.
